QueueContainer

The QueueContainer control displays the first visible element in a queue, with a small stack behind it to show that more elements are waiting.

Properties and Methods

  • CurrentElement: The first visible child. Only that child is used for child focus and input.
  • QueueElement / InsertElementAt: Adds a child to the queue or inserts it at a chosen index.
  • PopElement(): Removes and returns the first child without disposing it. Returns null when the queue is empty.
  • RemoveElementAt: Removes a child at the specified index without disposing it.
  • StackDirection / MaxStackDisplaySize: Sets the direction and maximum depth of the stack preview.

C# Example

Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples.

Output Example

Notes

PopElement removes the first child in the collection, even if it is hidden. In that case it can differ from CurrentElement, which uses the first visible child.

You can reuse a popped element by adding it to another owner. Dispose it when you no longer need it.

QueueContainer displays queued UI cards. It does not implement an audio play queue or automatically bind a key to advance to the next card.

The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement. While attached to a running window, update the control on the UI thread.
